method.controls: Compare unchanged, local gain, ordinary same-speech resampling, whole-file EQ and one different natural passage from the same reader. Refuse wrong reader, same-source 320 ms clock shift, and an earlier recording sharing only one six-second half. Real and synthetic replacements both count as physical-change positives. Mix at 0, -5 and -10 dB with identical background and gain per prompt.
method.gate: At -5 dB report at least four useful synthetic locations from at least two assessment readers and two zones, with no more than two flagged unchanged/gain/resampling/EQ controls in that condition, no wrong-reference admissions at any level, and no misplaced held positives at -5 dB. Use 0.30 IoU and 0.50 edit recall. Maintain distinct missing-match coverage. No confidence impact.
method.input: Exactly twelve seconds of continuous native aligned mono signed16 at 16 kHz, with a separately supplied earlier clean copy. Use six overlapping fixed six-second windows starting every 1.20 seconds. Keep the signed six-second calculation, match criteria and numeric point frozen.
method.rule: Require at least four of six accepted matches, including the first and last window. A reportable pair of six-second window results must come from adjacent windows and have at least half of the 720 ms interval in common. Select the stronger interval from the pair ranked by the smaller response and then earlier range. Compare also the best single flag on the same grid and the first six seconds of the original lane.
method.sources: Use the short-reference study's frozen source role identities, with twelve-second continuous source segments chosen by sample clock, exact publisher word alignment, and hash ranking. One early, middle and late edit per eligible reader where available. Competing speech comes from the role-disjoint recorded AMI sessions used in the short-reference study with independently selected continuous twelve-second excerpts. Exclude exact six-second prior cuts. Keep wrong-reference readers in the same role.
